paragraphs.text: And when they draw nigh unto Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sendeth two of his disciples,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote engizousin eis Hierosolyma eis Bēthphagē kai Bēthanian pros to Oros tōn Elaiōn, apostellei dyo tōn mathētōn autou

paragraphs.text: and saith unto them, Go your way into the village that is over against you: and straightway as ye enter into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon no man ever yet sat; loose him, and bring him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφʼ ὃν οὐδεὶς οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν· λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Hypagete eis tēn kōmēn tēn katenanti hymōn, kai euthys eisporeuomenoi eis autēn heurēsete pōlon dedemenon ephʼ hon oudeis oupō anthrōpōn ekathisen· lysate auton kai pherete.

paragraphs.text: And if any one say unto you, Why do ye this? say ye, The Lord hath need of him; and straightway he will send him back hither.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο; εἴπατε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει· καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει πάλιν ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean tis hymin eipē· Ti poieite touto; eipate hoti Ho kyrios autou chreian echei· kai euthys auton apostellei palin hōde.

paragraphs.text: And they went away, and found a colt tied at the door without in the open street; and they loose him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθον καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου, καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthon kai heuron pōlon dedemenon pros thyran exō epi tou amphodou, kai lyousin auton.

paragraphs.text: And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt?
paragraphs.original: καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς· Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον;
paragraphs.translit: kai tines tōn ekei hestēkotōn elegon autois· Ti poieite lyontes ton pōlon;

paragraphs.text: And they said unto them even as Jesus had said: and they let them go.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan autois kathōs eipen ho Iēsous· kai aphēkan autous.

paragraphs.text: And they bring the colt unto Jesus, and cast on him their garments; and he sat upon him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai pherousin ton pōlon pros ton Iēsoun, kai epiballousin autō ta himatia autōn, kai ekathisen epʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: And many spread their garments upon the way; and others branches, which they had cut from the fields.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλοὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai polloi ta himatia autōn estrōsan eis tēn hodon, alloi de stibadas kopsantes ek tōn agrōn.

paragraphs.text: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, Hosanna; Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord:
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον· Ὡσαννά· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου·
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi proagontes kai hoi akolouthountes ekrazon· Hōsanna· Eulogēmenos ho erchomenos en onomati kyriou·

paragraphs.text: Blessed [is] the kingdom that cometh, [the kingdom] of our father David: Hosanna in the highest.
paragraphs.original: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυίδ· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.
paragraphs.translit: Eulogēmenē hē erchomenē basileia tou patros hēmōn Dauid· Hōsanna en tois hypsistois.

paragraphs.text: And he entered into Jerusalem, into the temple; and when he had looked round about upon all things, it being now eventide, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eisēlthen eis Hierosolyma eis to hieron· kai periblepsamenos panta opse ēdē ousēs tēs hōras exēlthen eis Bēthanian meta tōn dōdeka.

paragraphs.text: And on the morrow, when they were come out from Bethany, he hungered.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai tē epaurion exelthontōn autōn apo Bēthanias epeinasen.

paragraphs.text: And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if haply he might find anything thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for it was not the season of figs.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα τι εὑρήσει ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα, ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν σύκων.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn sykēn apo makrothen echousan phylla ēlthen ei ara ti heurēsei en autē, kai elthōn epʼ autēn ouden heuren ei mē phylla, ho gar kairos ouk ēn sykōn.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit from thee henceforward for ever. And his disciples heard it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι. καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis eipen autē· Mēketi eis ton aiōna ek sou mēdeis karpon phagoi. kai ēkouon hoi mathētai autou.

paragraphs.text: And they come to Jerusalem: and he entered into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and them that bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold the doves;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai eis Hierosolyma. kai eiselthōn eis to hieron ērxato ekballein tous pōlountas kai tous agorazontas en tō hierō, kai tas trapezas tōn kollybistōn kai tas kathedras tōn pōlountōn tas peristeras katestrepsen

paragraphs.text: and he would not suffer that any man should carry a vessel through the temple.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk ēphien hina tis dienenkē skeuos dia tou hierou,

paragraphs.text: And he taught, and said unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations? but ye have made it a den of robbers.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai edidasken kai elegen autois· Ou gegraptai hoti Ho oikos mou oikos proseuchēs klēthēsetai pasin tois ethnesin; hymeis de pepoiēkate auton spēlaion lēstōn.

paragraphs.text: And the chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, for all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousan hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis, kai ezētoun pōs auton apolesōsin· ephobounto gar auton, pas gar ho ochlos exeplēsseto epi tē didachē autou.

paragraphs.text: And every evening he went forth out of the city.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hotan opse egeneto, exeporeuonto exō tēs poleōs.

paragraphs.text: And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai paraporeuomenoi prōi eidon tēn sykēn exērammenēn ek rhizōn.

paragraphs.text: And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Rabbi, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.
paragraphs.translit: kai anamnēstheis ho Petros legei autō· Rhabbi, ide hē sykē hēn katērasō exērantai.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Iēsous legei autois· Echete pistin theou·

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken up and cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that what he saith cometh to pass; he shall have it.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ πιστεύῃ ὅτι ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται, ἔσται αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti hos an eipē tō orei toutō· Arthēti kai blēthēti eis tēn thalassan, kai mē diakrithē en tē kardia autou alla pisteuē hoti ho lalei ginetai, estai autō.

paragraphs.text: Therefore I say unto you, All things whatsoever ye pray and ask for, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε, πιστεύετε ὅτι ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto legō hymin, panta hosa proseuchesthe kai aiteisthe, pisteuete hoti elabete, kai estai hymin.

paragraphs.text: And whensoever ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have aught against any one; that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅταν στήκετε προσευχόμενοι, ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hotan stēkete proseuchomenoi, aphiete ei ti echete kata tinos, hina kai ho patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois aphē hymin ta paraptōmata hymōn.

paragraphs.text: [But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your trespasses.]
And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai palin eis Hierosolyma. kai en tō hierō peripatountos autou erchontai pros auton hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis kai hoi presbyteroi

paragraphs.text: and they said unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? or who gave thee this authority to do these things?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; ἢ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς;
paragraphs.translit: kai elegon autō· En poia exousia tauta poieis; ē tis soi edōken tēn exousian tautēn hina tauta poiēs;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, I will ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον, καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι, καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Eperōtēsō hymas hena logon, kai apokrithēte moi, kai erō hymin en poia exousia tauta poiō·

paragraphs.text: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men? answer me.
paragraphs.original: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; ἀποκρίθητέ μοι.
paragraphs.translit: to baptisma to Iōannou ex ouranou ēn ē ex anthrōpōn; apokrithēte moi.

paragraphs.text: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; He will say, Why then did ye not believe him?
paragraphs.original: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες· Τί εἴπωμεν; ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: kai dielogizonto pros heautous legontes· Ti eipōmen; ean eipōmen· Ex ouranou, erei· Dia ti oun ouk episteusate autō;

paragraphs.text: But should we say, From men--they feared the people: for all verily held John to be a prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;— ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ὄχλον, ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάννην ὄντως ὅτι προφήτης ἦν.
paragraphs.translit: alla eipōmen· Ex anthrōpōn;— ephobounto ton ochlon, hapantes gar eichon ton Iōannēn ontōs hoti prophētēs ēn.

paragraphs.text: And they answered Jesus and say, We know not. And Jesus saith unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokrithentes tō Iēsou legousin· Ouk oidamen. kai ho Iēsous legei autois· Oude egō legō hymin en poia exousia tauta poiō.
